summary: A task that hits the dispatch requeue cap with approved reviews and a mechanical stop is re-enqueued as a fresh manifest; names AISDLC-676

options.description: remove-verdict --from failed, then enqueue a fresh manifest (retryCount 0), then write-resume-signal with the mechanical-stop note on claim; the failed manifest's retry history is kept in the dispatch digest. Applies to AISDLC-676 now and to any later task whose cap-hitting stops were all mechanical (push, rebase, patch-id moved, missing leaf, manifest mismatch, environment-only test failure) with reviewer approvals on the current head.
Raise the requeue retry limit for the task (cli-dispatch requeue --retry-limit); the CLI refuses values above 2 by design (mistake guard), so this needs a code change first.
Land post-drain item 2 (requeue cap exempts mechanical failures) as a code change before touching 676; 676 waits ~1 day for a one-line policy the record below states.
Leave 676 parked in failed/ until the drain ends.

body: Rubric. Problem: the dispatch board caps requeues of one manifest at 2 (mistake guard against a task that keeps failing on its own defect). AISDLC-676 (#1360) hit the cap after three stops that were all mechanical and post-approval: DEC-0149 verifier revert (operator decision), then the hand-run test-reviewer's transcript leaf not emitted, twice (DEC-0151). Its reviews are approved on the current head. Research: CI systems separate 'retry budget' (flaky/infra) from 'failure budget' (red tests): GitHub Actions re-run of failed jobs, Buildkite automatic retry on exit-status classes, Bazel flaky-test attempts; all exempt infra-class failures from the failure count. The board's cap does not yet distinguish the classes (post-drain item 2). Options and tradeoffs: fresh-manifest keeps the guard intact for real failures (the failed manifest and its count remain in history) and costs nothing; raise-cap is refused by the CLI; fix-cap-first delays 676 behind a code PR and reviewer round for a policy this record already states; park wastes approved review work and leaves a trust-sensitive PR (RFC-0052) stale. Recommendation: fresh-manifest. Counter-argument: 'a fresh manifest is the cap bypass the guard exists to prevent, and dispatch will apply it liberally.' Rebuttal: the record scopes it to stops that are all mechanical with approvals on the current head, which the executor's verdict notes and leaves make checkable; a capped task with any real test or review failure stays parked and goes to the planner. Class (a): reversible (the manifest can be removed), task-local, tightens or loosens no trust-chain control (reviews and attestation are unchanged). Five-step: requirement questioned = 'every requeue counts against the cap' (set by AISDLC-800's author 2026-10-10 before mechanical stops were understood) - narrowed, nothing added; item 2 later makes it code.
